name: gpython-444ae5ed-blind30-ots
instr:
# go-python/gpython: wrong answers across numbers, text and source preparation, without a test suite

This is an interpreter for a dynamic scripting language, driven either from a shell or embedded in a larger program, and it now gets a great many ordinary things wrong. Starting it from a shell with the path of a program to run no longer runs that program: the version greeting is printed, then the platform and toolchain lines, and then it sits waiting for typed input at the interactive prompt, so nothing the program was supposed to print ever appears.

The repository has received 30 separate undocumented edits.

Ordinary arithmetic is unreliable in several unrelated ways. Multiplying two numbers that each carry a real and an imaginary part gives their quotient rather than their product, so even squaring one answers with an unexpected sign and magnitude. Multiplying a very large whole number by a small one wraps around, occasionally to a negative value, instead of giving the exact result, while products of two moderately sized whole numbers are still right. Adding up every number in a sequence with the standard total-taking call does not produce the total at all; the call fails instead of returning a number. Asking for the largest or the smallest member of a sequence fails as well, rather than handing back a member, both in the plain case and when a per-member transform is supplied. Asking for the natural logarithm of the gamma of a positive whole number is turned down as out
